title: Speaking: interviews and role-play
competency: Ask and answer questions about economic activities in an interview and a role-play.

keywords.def: A meeting where one person asks another questions to find out information.
A question that starts with a question word: what, where, why, how, who, when, which.

en.text: An interview is a meeting where one person asks questions to find out information. Good interviewers use Wh-questions (What, Where, Why, How, Which) because they invite full answers, not just yes or no. In the role-play, Akelo asks Lucy questions about her part-time job and then gives advice.

am.text: ቃለ መጠይቅ መረጃ ለማግኘት ጥያቄ የሚጠየቅበት ነው። "ምን፣ የት፣ ለምን፣ እንዴት" የሚሉ ጥያቄዎች ሙሉ መልስ ያስገኛሉ።

screens.title: A good question
screens.ask: Which question gets a longer, more useful answer in an interview?
opts: What economic activities do people do in your village?
screens.after: The Wh-question. "What…?" invites a full answer; the others can be answered "yes" or "no".

screens.title: Interview questions
paras: 1. What are the economic activities people do in your village?
2. Which economic activities do you like most? Why?
3. Which of the economic activities do you think are more profitable or less profitable?
4. Which economic activities employ more people in your area? Give examples.

screens.title: Role-play: Akelo and Lucy
paras: Akelo: Hi, Lucy! How is it going?  Lucy: Fine, thanks, and you?
Akelo: Where are you going?  Lucy: To the library. I have to finish the assignment for tomorrow's class.
Akelo: Why don't you do it at home?  Lucy: I have a part-time job in the evening, so when I get home, I'll be too tired.
Akelo: Where do you work?  Lucy: I work in a café.
Akelo: Why do you like the job?  Lucy: It's interesting. I really enjoy working with people and get extra money.
Akelo: How is the pay?  Lucy: The pay's alright. I get 15 Birr an hour. I would like to earn more to buy a new laptop and a smartphone.
Akelo: And how would you do that?  Lucy: I'll try to pick up as many extra shifts as I can.
Akelo: What about your studies? How would you manage your time?  Lucy: Well, I don't know yet. I might take fewer courses next semester.
Akelo: I wouldn't do that if I were you. You should make your studies the first priority. What if your parents know about it?
Lucy: Ugh. You're right. Thanks for your advice, Akelo. See you later.

screens.text: Akelo says, "I wouldn't do that if I were you." What is he doing?
